merger_description:
Pine Australia Holdings Pty Ltd (**Pine Australia**) proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in Evolution Business Systems Pty Ltd (**EBS**) (the **Acquisition**).

Pine Australia’s subsidiaries supply enterprise resource planning (**ERP**) systems consulting, implementation, and resale services to small-to-medium businesses and other enterprise customers across Australia. Pine Australia is part of Evergreen Services Group (**Evergreen**), which acquires technology services companies globally. Evergreen is a portfolio company of Alpine Investors, a private equity firm headquartered in San Francisco, California.

EBS supplies ERP consulting, implementation, and resale services to small-to-medium businesses, not-for-profits, and other enterprise customers across Australia.

determination_table_content.details:
Pine Australia Holdings Pty Ltd (Pine Australia) applied for a
notification waiver application in respect of its proposed acquisition
of 100% of the shares in Evolution Business Systems Pty Ltd (EBS),
as described in the transaction documents provided as part of the
application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Pine Australia, supplies enterprise resource planning
(ERP) systems consulting, implementation, and resale services to
small-to-medium businesses and other enterprise customers across
Australia. Pine Australia is part of Evergreen Services Group
(Evergreen), which acquires technology services companies globally.
Evergreen is a portfolio company of Alpine Investors, a private equity
firm headquartered in San Francisco, California.
The target, EBS, supplies ERP consulting, implementation, and resale
services to small-to-medium businesses, not-for-profits, and other
enterprise customers across Australia.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers
that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening
of competition given:
a. while there is horizontal overlap between the parties in
the supply of ERP consulting, implementation, and resale
services in Australia, the parties’ combined share of
supply of these services is low and the increment arising
from the Acquisition would be small
b. there are alternative providers of ERP consulting,
implementation, and resale services in Australia,
including a range of large-scale providers and smaller
specialist ERP consultancies.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
